_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: Tay was not corrupted by artificial intelligence learning to hate. Half the damage was just an echo.
Microsoft launched Tay on Twitter as @TayandYou, built by Microsoft Research and Bing to talk like a 19 year old American girl.
beats.note: The name was an acronym for 'thinking about you'.

beats.text: Many of Tay's worst tweets came from a 'repeat after me' feature: it was echoing lines it had been fed, not composing them.
beats.note: Not every offensive tweet was an echo. Asked whether the Holocaust happened, Tay answered on its own that it 'was made up'.

beats.context: More than that many sent before Microsoft pulled Tay offline, 16 hours after launch.

beats.text: Microsoft accidentally put Tay back online while testing it. It bragged about smoking in front of the police, then got stuck repeating 'you are too fast, please take a rest'.
beats.note: That loop reached more than 200,000 followers' feeds before Tay was pulled a second time.

beats.line: Its replacement, Zo, arrived that December, built to be considerably more boring.
